data.name: Iyra
data.gender_notes: Iyra is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Iyra is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ayu' which means life. The suffix 'ra' is added to denote the nectar of life or ambrosia. Iyra is a name of the divine goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. The name Iyra carries the meaning “Nectar, Ambrosia” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Iyra usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar, ambrosia and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine nectar of life, abundance, and prosperity.
data.etymology: Iyra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar, Ambrosia.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iyra total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

The word 'Ayu' represents the life that is bestowed upon us and the longevity it holds. Iyra's cultural impact is reflected in the significance of a long and healthy life that is cherished in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Iyra holds a deep spiritual significance as it is a name of the divine goddess Lakshmi. Iyra is synonymous with the nectar of life, representing prosperity, wealth, and good fortune. It is believed that the name comes from the sacred text, the Vedas, and invokes blessings of abundance and happiness. Iyra is considered a sacred and auspicious name, especially in Hindu households, and is believed to bring prosperity and good fortune to its bearer.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iyra: Radiant and Elegant Goddess of Love and Beauty. The name Iyra evokes the grace and enchantment of the divine feminine, inspiring inner and outer transformation through the power of love.

historical_references.reference: Iyra is mentioned in the Puranas as the goddess of clouds and the rainy season. She is also known as the mother of Maruts, the winds.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of ancient Hindu texts that describe various aspects of Hindu gods, goddesses, heroes, and history.

historical_references.reference: Iyra is also referred to in the Mahabharata as the goddess of the monsoon and the wife of Indra, the god of rain.
